full_zh: 背景：一个即将离职的实习生留下一个机器学习费用异常检测器，它只在 QA 环境跑过。顺着惯性，应该接着做下去。
判断：我没有接着做，而是写了一份 go/no-go 评估。我把 QA 和生产放在一起比：QA 只有 6 个合成商户、不到 10 亿行，生产是 18,140 个商户、约 15,000 种 plan 组合，峰值一天约 7.6 亿行。它的推理是逐行 numpy，在生产规模必然超时，而 QA 永远暴露不了这一点。
保全：我把“会随实习生离职消失的”和“可以从代码重建的”分开。代码、terraform、训练配方（固定 seed）都能重建，唯一不可再生的是分析师的 disposition 标注，所以我在他离开前把标注导出。
分阶段：Phase 1 只上确定性规则（金额等于费率乘数量加固定费），纯 SQL，Snowflake 本来就能处理几十亿行。Phase 2 是模型重训加推理重构，需要 2 到 3 个月，放在明确的 go/no-go gate 后面。同时冻结 Slack 告警和 CI/CD 工作，直到 gate 给出 go。
结果与学到：不可替代的标注保住了，便宜的防御层有了清晰路径，数字是我自己评估文档里的量级，我会如实说明还没在生产复核。我宁可停一个项目，也不上线一个凌晨 3 点呼叫团队的项目。
full_en: I inherited an ML fee-anomaly detector from an intern who was leaving. It had only ever run in QA, and the easy path was to keep building. Instead I wrote a go/no-go assessment. QA had six synthetic merchants and under a billion rows; production is about eighteen thousand merchants, around fifteen thousand plan combinations, and up to about 760 million rows on a peak day. The serving design was a per-row numpy forward pass, which would time out at that scale, and QA could never have shown it. I split the problem into what disappears when the intern leaves versus what's reproducible from code: only the analysts' labels were irreplaceable, so I got those exported before their last day. Then a phased plan. Phase one ships only the deterministic consistency rule as pure SQL, which Snowflake handles at billions of rows. Phase two, retraining and a new serving design, is two to three months and sits behind an explicit go/no-go gate. I froze the Slack alerting and CI/CD work until the gate says go. I'd rather stop a project than ship one that pages the team at 3 a.m. These numbers come from my own assessment and I haven't re-verified them in production.

hook.example: QA was under a billion rows and production is tens of billions, so we're off by an order of magnitude.

hook.zh: 测试环境与生产环境的差距
hook.example: The gap between QA and production hid the timeout completely.
My numbers are back-of-the-envelope figures from the assessment, not production-verified.

starl.example: I put Phase 2 behind an explicit go/no-go gate that my manager could audit.
A phased rollout let us ship the cheap SQL rule first and defer the ML work.
I froze the Slack alerting work until the gate says go.

followups.example: We had no ground truth for precision, so a shadow run was the only honest test.
At a 99.5 percent threshold we'd have produced millions of alerts a day, which is alert fatigue by design.
I didn't rank priorities by sunk cost, I ranked them by risk-adjusted value.

relp.example: I said no with a written assessment rather than with opinion.
The analyst labels were the one irreversible loss, so exporting them was the urgent step.
I'd rather stop a project than ship one that gets the team paged at 3 a.m.

full.example: I made the go/no-go call on the detector with the precision numbers in front of me.
I argued to phase the rollout instead of switching everything on at once.
For an alert people get paged on, I'd choose precision over recall.

senior.q: How would you prove the detector is precise enough before turning it on for real alerts?
senior.why: 面试官在探：没有 ground truth 时你怎么设计可信的评估。
framework: 先说 shadow mode：只记录不告警，持续跑一段时间
让分析师对一个抽样的结果打标，建立精确率的估计
按商户和费用类型分层抽样，避免被前两个大商户主导
提前写下放行的精确率阈值和每日告警量上限
senior.best_practice: 异常检测没有现成标签，精确率只能靠人工标注的抽样来估。分层抽样是关键，因为 QA 里前两个商户占 97% 的行，不分层的话结论会被少数大户主导。阈值要在看数据之前定，否则是事后合理化。

terms.zh: 影子模式：只运行不生效
terms.example: I'd run the model in shadow mode and let analysts label a sample.
Stratified sampling matters because two merchants made up 97 percent of the QA rows.

senior.q: The team wanted to ship the detector as planned. How do you hold a no-go position without becoming the blocker?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你在压力下坚持立场，同时保持合作与可逆性的方式。
framework: 把分歧变成可检验的事实：用文档写清风险、数字和假设
给出替代路径而不是只说不：Phase 1 马上就能交付价值
说明什么证据会让我改变结论，也就是 go 的条件
把决定交给能独立判断的人，保证过程可审计
senior.best_practice: 只说不会变成阻碍，给出能立刻交付的 Phase 1 加上明确的 go 条件，别人才能接受停下 Phase 2。写成文档而不是靠情绪，是为了让上级能独立判断；承认可能错，并写明什么证据会推翻我，也是 Have Backbone 的一部分。

terms.example: I disagreed with data, a written assessment, not with a gut feeling.
I wrote the exit criteria for Phase 2 so the decision wasn't open-ended.

senior.q: What would you do to make per-row inference work at 760 million rows a day if the business did want the model?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你对规模化推理的工程思路，是否能从逐行改成批量化。
framework: 先把瓶颈定位清楚：逐行 Python 调用和数据搬运，而不是模型本身
把推理推到数据旁边：用 Snowflake 的向量化 UDF 或把模型计算改成 set-based
先用规则过滤出候选，只对少量候选跑模型
上线前用生产量级数据做压力测试，并设超时与降级
senior.best_practice: 逐行 numpy 的问题是调用开销和数据移动，不是算力不够。把计算放到数据所在的地方、先用便宜的规则缩小范围，就能把规模降几个数量级。这也是为什么 Phase 1 的纯 SQL 规则本身就能挡住大部分问题。

terms.zh: 基于集合的批量处理，而非逐行
terms.example: Moving from per-row to set-based processing is the first change I'd make.

terms.zh: 把计算推到数据所在之处
terms.example: I'd push compute to the data instead of pulling rows out to Python.

senior.q: What would you do differently, and how do you prevent handoffs like this from becoming a risk in the first place?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你能否从一次个案抽出组织层面的机制。
framework: 承认问题：一个人带着关键标注和只在 QA 跑过的代码离开
提议实习项目的 exit checklist：标注导出、环境说明、生产准备度评估
要求任何 ML 项目在立项时写下生产规模假设
更早做评估，而不是在最后一周才发现
senior.best_practice: 这件事的根因是项目没有生产准备度的检查点，不是某个人的失误。把评估前移到立项时，并把不可再生的资产（标注）列进离职清单，才能让下一次不依赖我临时发现。下次我会更早发起评估，而不是等到离职前。

terms.example: I'd add irreplaceable assets like labels to the handoff checklist.
A production readiness review at kickoff would have surfaced the scale gap earlier.
